# EQUAL Generic Key Publication

This repository exists solely to publish the EQUAL Generic private key
in the event that EQUAL Research and Innovations Ltd permanently
ceases operating.

**This repository currently contains no private key.** EQUAL is
operating normally. Nothing here can be used to decrypt anything at
this time.

## What this is

EQUAL-Encryptor is a quantum-safe file encryption product built by
EQUAL Research and Innovations Ltd
(https://sites.google.com/view/equal-r-and-i/home). To protect against
the risk of files becoming permanently inaccessible if the company
ever stops operating, EQUAL maintains a dead-man's-switch: if the
service goes silent for an extended period, this repository will be
updated with the Generic private key used for all unrestricted
EQUAL-Encryptor files.

## The Generic public key, published now, in advance

The private half of this key does not exist here yet, and may never
need to. Its **public** half, and its fingerprint, are published below
now, while EQUAL is operating normally -- so that if the private key
is ever published here, anyone can verify it's genuinely the matching
half of this same key, not a substitute planted after the fact.

**SHA-256 fingerprint:**
```
a686a099678a812a369c3a8d02541f4566a2d394d58b944141cbad0cbcf2862c
```

**Public key (DER, base64-encoded):**

## What will be published here, if this ever activates

- The Generic **private** key (ML-KEM-1024, DER format) -- its public
  half is already shown above; when the private key appears, its own
  public half can be independently re-derived and compared against the
  fingerprint above as a check
- The exact date this was published
- Instructions for using it to recover an unrestricted file offline,
  without needing EQUAL's servers at all

This will **only** ever cover unrestricted files. Files restricted to
specific recipients are never recoverable using this key -- see
EQUAL-Encryptor's own documentation on personal recovery keys for that
separate case, which relies on a key only the original sender ever
held.
